'''Charles "Chuck" Joel Stone''' (July 13, 1936 – April 16, 2019) was an American statistician and mathematician.

==Early life==
Charles Joel Stone was born and raised in [[Los Angeles]].<ref name=recollections>{{cite journal|arxiv=1101.0941|doi=10.1214/10-AOAS431|title=Selected recollections of my relationship with Leo Breiman|year=2010|last1=Stone|first1=Charles J.|journal=The Annals of Applied Statistics|volume=4|issue=4|s2cid=62578779}}</ref> After secondary school at [[North Hollywood High School]], Stone  graduated with a [[Bachelor of Science]] in science from the [[California Institute of Technology]] in 1958.<ref name="cal">{{Cite web |url=https://campuspubs.library.caltech.edu/2539/3/June_13%252C_1958.pdf |title=California Institute of Technology Sixth-fourth Annual Commencement Exercise |date=1958 |website=[[California Institute of Technology]] |access-date=2021-07-25}}</ref><ref name=obit>{{cite web|author=Olshen, Richard A.|author2=Bickel, Peter|author3=Evans, Steven N.|year=2020|title=In Memoriam. Charles Joel Stone, Professor of Statistics, Emeritus, UC Berkeley|website=Academic Senate, University of California|url=https://senate.universityofcalifornia.edu/in-memoriam/files/chuck-stone.html}}</ref> He then matriculated at [[Stanford University]], where in 1961 he received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in statistics. His PhD thesis ''Limit Theorems for Birth and Death Processes and Diffusion Processes'' was supervised by [[Samuel Karlin]].<ref name=MathGen>{{MathGenealogy|id=26991}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Charles Joel Stone|website=Alumni, Statistics Department, Stanford University|url=https://statistics.stanford.edu/people/charles-joel-stone}}</ref>

==Career==
From 1962 to 1964 Stone was an assistant professor in the mathematics department of [[Cornell University]]. From 1964 1981 to he was a faculty member of the mathematics department of UCLA ([[University of California, Los Angeles]]), where he worked extensively with [[Leo Breiman]] (who moved to Berkeley in 1980) and Sidney Charles Port (born 1935).<ref name=recollections/> In the statistics department of the [[University of California, Berkeley]], Stone was from 1981 a full professor, a position which he held until his retirement as professor emeritus.<ref name=obit/>

When they were professors at UCLA, Stone and Breiman consulted for Technology Services Corporation in Santa Monica. Based on their work, they co-authored a 1978 technical report, ''Parsimonious Binary Classification Trees'', Elaborating on the report, in 1984 they published, with two more co-authors, [[Jerome H. Friedman]] and Richard Allen Oshlen (born 1942), a greatly expended version entitled ''Classification and Regression Trees''.<ref name=obit/>

In addition to research on statistical algorithms, Stone did research on potential theory, "local limit theorems, weak convergence of stochastic processes, and renewal theory."<ref name=obit/>

Stone was a Guggenheim Fellow for the academic year 1980–1981.<ref>{{cite web|title=Charles J. Stone|website=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/charles-j-stone/}}</ref> In 1986 he was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Berkeley, California]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Stone, C. J.|title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, August 3–11, 1986, Berkeley, California|year=1986|volume=2|pages=1052–1056|chapter=A nonparametric framework for statistical modelling}}</ref> He was elected a Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] in 1970 <ref>{{cite web|title=Stone, Charles J.|website=Scientific Legacy Database, Institute of Mathematical Statistics|url=https://imstat.org/scientific-legacy-database/?person_name=Stone%2C+Charles+J.&person_id=992}}</ref> and a Fellow of the Class of 2013 (announced in 2012) of the [[American Mathematical Society]].
He was elected a Member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 1993.<ref>{{cite web|title=Charles J. Stone|website=Member Directory, National Academy of Sciences|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/charles-j-stone-ohh3mu/}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In June 1966 he married Barbara L. Cohn in Los Angeles. They had two sons.<ref name=obit/>

==Death==
Stone died on April 16, 2019.<ref name="obit"/>
